notes: Read all 60 source lines before editing. L1 `import { useEffect, useState } from 'react'` kept verbatim (identical in React Native). L3-23 the original JSDoc (matchMedia contract, the three mobile-aware example queries, the SSR/no-window 'false then upgrade' safety note, and the modern-addEventListener-never-deprecated-addListener note) is preserved and expanded with the native adaptation block at the top of the output file.

L24-30 hook signature `useMediaQuery(query: string): boolean` and its lazy useState initializer are preserved. Web initializer was `typeof window === 'undefined' || typeof window.matchMedia !== 'function' ? false : window.matchMedia(query).matches`. Native equivalent: getMatchMedia() (a globalThis.matchMedia probe that needs no DOM lib and no `window` reference — both untyped/forbidden in native) returns the bound fn on react-native-web-in-browser so the initializer stays `mm(query).matches` (exact web parity), else falls back to evaluateQuery(query, readEnv(false)) where reduceMotion starts false to mirror the web SSR default.

L32-47 the useEffect is preserved with [query] deps. The matchMedia branch is a 1:1 port of the web effect: build mql = mm(query); setMatches(mql.matches) (the same 'sync once in case first-paint default disagrees' comment from L37-39); listener (event: {matches:boolean}) => setMatches(event.matches) (L42); mql.addEventListener('change', listener) (L43, modern API only, never addListener per L19-22); cleanup returns mql.removeEventListener('change', listener) (L44-46).

L26/L33 the web `typeof window === 'undefined' || typeof window.matchMedia !== 'function'` guard (return false / early-return) is reproduced by getMatchMedia() returning null on native; instead of the web's no-op, native provides the documented explicit fallback required by the conversion contract for browser-only behavior — Dimensions (width/height/orientation), Platform.OS (pointer coarse/fine + hover, ios/android => touch), and AccessibilityInfo (prefers-reduced-motion) drive evaluateQuery. Width re-evaluates via Dimensions.addEventListener('change', recompute); reduce-motion via AccessibilityInfo.addEventListener('reduceMotionChanged', ...); both subscriptions .remove() on unmount, plus a `cancelled` guard, matching L44-46 cleanup semantics.

SSR/first-paint safety from L14-17 preserved: AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled() is async so reduce-motion resolves to false synchronously (web SSR default) then upgrades on the first effect tick via .then(); .catch keeps the false default. The three documented example queries are all covered: '(max-width: 640px)' -> width<=640 via Dimensions; '(pointer: coarse)' -> IS_TOUCH_PLATFORM; '(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)' -> env.reduceMotion. evaluateQuery also handles comma (OR), `and` (AND), min/max-width, min/max-height, orientation, any-pointer/hover/any-hover; unknown/non-derivable features (e.g. prefers-color-scheme) return false, mirroring web matchMedia's no-match default.

L49 `return matches` preserved verbatim. L52-55 `useIsMobile()` -> useMediaQuery('(max-width: 640px)') and L57-60 `useIsCoarsePointer()` -> useMediaQuery('(pointer: coarse)') ported verbatim with their JSDoc. No behavior, state name (`matches`/`setMatches`), or exported-API drift. No unit-suffixed fields are involved (this is a non-unit utility hook), so the SI cutover contract is unaffected.

Native-safety: no DOM modules, no `window`, no browser HTML elements, no Recharts/Leaflet/framer-motion, and no old web UI components are imported — only `react` (useEffect/useState) and `react-native` (AccessibilityInfo, Dimensions, Platform). The matchMedia bridge is a runtime globalThis capability probe (the same idiom as the web `typeof window.matchMedia` guard), not a DOM import, and a local MediaQueryListLike structural type keeps the DOM `lib` out of native output. A focused Jest test (__tests__/UseMediaQueryParity.test.tsx) drives the hook through a probe component: verifies max-width true/false against spied Dimensions, useIsMobile, useIsCoarsePointer true on the ios test platform, min-width, prefers-reduced-motion default false, and reactive re-evaluation on a Dimensions 'change' emit.
